results.title: S. Korea's UN envoy named co-chair of global AI governance dialogue
results.content: WASHINGTON — South Korea's ambassador to the United Nations has been appointed as co-chair of a U.N. initiative aimed at promoting international cooperation on artificial intelligence (AI) governance, according to the U.N. website Tuesday. Ambassador Cha Ji-hoon was appointed alongside Mutryce Agatha Williams, the permanent representative of Saint Kitts and Nevis, by the president of the U.N. General Assembly on Friday to lead preparations for the 2027 Global Dialogue on AI Governance. The dialogue, scheduled for May 3-4, 2027, will bring together governments and other stakeholders to discuss international cooperation on AI governance, including opportunities and challenges associated with the rapidly developing technology. results.title: US cites evolving 'threat environment' amid debate over OPCON transition to S. Korea
results.content: WASHINGTON — A senior U.S. official said Tuesday the requirements for the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) to South Korea remain unchanged but stressed that the threat environment on the Korean Peninsula was evolving faster than ever before. "The fundamental requirements for OPCON transfer have not changed. But the threat environment is evolving faster now than ever before," the official told Yonhap News Agency in response to a media inquiry on the state of the bilateral OPCON transition review process. "Together, we must be prepared to deter and defeat all regional threats to the alliance," the official, who asked not to be identified, added. The official appeared to reflect concerns over evolving threats posed by advancements in Pyongyang's missile and nuclear programs. results.title: Rushed single-stock leveraged ETF rollout leaves questions of responsibility unanswered
results.content: Policymakers have yet to explain who decided to introduce single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or why their reviews were expedited, even as retail investors have sustained more than 2 trillion won ($1.5 billion) in losses on the products tracking Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. The funds have also drawn criticism for amplifying stock market volatility. At a National Assembly audit Monday, Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Gov. Lee Chan-jin acknowledged that the products underwent unusually rapid reviews to meet a policy timetable. But he offered no concrete explanation of who set that timetable or on what grounds. These ETFs were made possible by a government decision to ease regulations. An amendment to the enforcement decree of the Capital Markets Act cleared the Cabinet on April 21. results.title: Grammy boycott debate turns toward K-pop acts that submitted
results.content: Fans were angry at the Grammys/Recording Academy for creating the new Asian pop category, but some of that anger is now directed at K-pop acts that reportedly submitted for the category. The academy has not officially disclosed which acts entered the category, though some have been named in local media outlets. Criticism has mounted in some online fan communities, with people questioning whether the acts should compete in a category that many see as discriminatory and some even asking whether they really want to win a "racist award." Others have countered that pursuing a Grammy nomination is a practical choice for artists. The debate traces back to June, when the academy announced that Best Asian Pop Music Performance, one of five new categories, will debut at the 69th Grammy Awards in February 2027. results.content: The woman who has accused seven students of raping her at a Cornell University fraternity house has weighed in on a looming faculty vote of no confidence in the school’s leadership, saying the university’s president questioned why she waited to report being assaulted — an alleged remark she said left her feeling “unsupported and disbelieved.” Her case has prompted student protests, renewed scrutiny of the university’s disciplinary system and a state investigation into the alleged assault. results.title: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country
results.content: TEHRAN — Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday told the visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Tehran would not allow nuclear material to leave the country, according to state TV. "Not even a tiny bit of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran; such materials constitute a major asset and national wealth for the Iranian people, intended for use within the country," said Rezaei, Iran's secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. "There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust — a process that must begin with the fulfilment of Iran's conditions," he added. Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf made similar remarks to Munir, who is in Tehran as part of a renewed push to mediate a peace deal between the Islamic republic and the United States. results.title: Zelensky, US envoys hold Oslo talks as Ukraine claims US missile holdup
results.content: OSLO — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks in Oslo with top U.S. envoys on Tuesday in a bid to get strained relations with Washington "on a more constructive path", Norway said. "Ukraine is working for peace. I thank our partners for their support!" Zelensky said in a social media post after his arrival in the Norwegian capital. Zelensky handed U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff an award in the Norwegian government's official residence, before posing with Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, according to footage accompanying the Ukrainian leader's post. Witkoff's fellow U.S. envoy Jared Kushner — U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law — was also taking part in the negotiations but was doing so remotely because of illness, according to the NTB agency. results.content: LONDON — Prince Harry has said he wants his disagreements with his brother Prince William and his father King Charles III to “work out." results.title: US bill calls for updating list of critical Golden Dome missile defense assets
results.content: WASHINGTON — A Republican U.S. lawmaker has introduced legislation calling for an update to the Pentagon's list of critical assets supporting President Donald Trump's Golden Dome missile defense initiative, citing growing missile threats from China and Russia and increased security cooperation among U.S. adversaries, including North Korea. Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) introduced the bill to the House of Representatives on Oct. 6, directing the secretary of defense to update the Pentagon's Critical Asset List to incorporate facilities and systems essential to the development, deployment and operation of Golden Dome. The legislation was referred to the House Armed Services Committee. The bill calls for including space-based sensors and interceptors, associated ground control stations, ground-based missile defense facilities and critical command-and-control infrastructure in the updated list. results.title: Wild West Wing? Turmoil revives memories of Trump 1.0
results.content: WASHINGTON — After a relatively disciplined start to Donald Trump's second term, the White House is grappling with signs of turmoil that have revived memories of his first chaotic presidency. From the extraordinary departure of his new press secretary after five days to questions about the future of his chief of staff, there have been a series of upheavals in recent weeks. The ructions come at the worst possible time for Trump, with many Republicans fearing that the president's dismal polling will drag on their chances in next month's midterm elections. The White House strongly denies there is infighting in what US media called the "Wild Wild West Wing" — with the fiercest pushback reserved for reports that Trump was looking to replace Susie Wiles, his ultra-loyal chief of staff. results.title: US stocks rise after companies deliver strong profits and oil prices retreat
results.content: NEW YORK — The U.S. stock market is rising Tuesday following strong profit reports for Equifax, Hasbro and other companies, while oil prices ease back after nearing their highest levels since the war with Iran began. The S&P 500 added 0.4 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 518 points, or 1 percent, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, while more swings for the artificial-intelligence industry had the Nasdaq composite up a more modest 0.2 percent. Stock prices tend to follow the path of corporate profits over the long term, and several companies delivered results for the latest quarter that were better than analysts expected. Big expectations for growth generally are what have allowed the U.S. stock market to hit records recently despite worries about high inflation, higher interest rates and other challenges weighing on Wall Street. results.title: How are French police identifying looters? Social media is key
results.content: PARIS — France's police striving to identify and arrest looters who shattered shops in last weekend's unrest are relying on one tool to trigger their forensic follow-up: social media. "We are working the social networks... then we go over all that with our own tools, to see if the crimes seen on social media correspond with the crimes we're studying," said an officer seated in a special operations room with 10 screens in front of him. The officer, identified only by his first name, Bruno, was seated in a gamer-style chair, pushing a mouse around as looked closely at a video. He said he was convinced he had identified a group of four youths who took part in the looting that had scarred Paris streets. results.title: Paris curfew to continue on Tuesday, could be prolonged for as long as needed
results.content: PARIS — The limited curfew conditions set up for France's capital in the wake of last weekend's violent protests will continue on Tuesday evening and may stay in place for as long as deemed necessary, wrote the Paris police department on X on Tuesday. The curfew lasts from 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) until 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) local time, and mainly covers the Republique and Halles areas of the capital.

results.title: Protesting truck drivers put Italy's pasta production at risk
results.content: MILAN — The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories. There are also growing concerns about food supplies in Rome, as transport bottlenecks hamper deliveries from southern Italy to the capital. Italian agriculture lobby group Confagricoltura warned that producers in Sicily would have to destroy large quantities of perishable products if transportation did not resume. Pasta maker Rummo, based in the Campania region, said on Tuesday it had suspended production after running out of ingredients. Almost all major pasta producers in the neighbouring region of Puglia, which together with Campania and Sicily form the heartland of Italy's pasta production, are facing similar difficulties, CEO Cosimo Rummo told daily la Repubblica. results.title: China says US' DeepSeek ban disregards Xi-Trump consensus
results.content: BEIJING — China's commerce ministry on Tuesday criticised a U.S. government order banning Chinese AI model DeepSeek from federal agency IT systems, saying it harmed Chinese firms' interests and disregarded understandings reached by the countries' leaders. In a statement, the ministry urged the U.S. to "immediately correct wrong practices ... and revoke relevant discriminatory restrictive measures," adding that Beijing would closely monitor developments and "take all necessary measures" to safeguard its interests. The U.S. Homeland Security Department on Monday ordered the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services using the Chinese AI model from civilian federal agency IT systems. results.title: S. Korean firm's debut plunge adds to investor concerns about AI spending
results.content: A 32 percent drop in shares of South Korea's Elice Group on Tuesday renewed investor concerns about the sustainability and the payoff cycle for the vast amount of capital pouring into the AI buildout amid growing scrutiny of company valuations. The plunge in shares of the provider of AI arcloud services as well as AI-based education and business software made it the worst debut ever in South Korea for a company that raised more than $100 million in an IPO, according to Dealogic data. Elice raised 201.1 billion won ($150 million) in its IPO, and said that it planned to spend most of the proceeds on launching portable modular data centres and related infrastructure. results.title: France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
results.content: PARIS — France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence. "The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17. In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable. results.title: Ugly loss by KBO champions closes book on iconic stadium
results.content: As the defending South Korean baseball champion LG Twins bowed out early in the postseason Tuesday night, the exit also closed the book on their iconic home park in the capital city, Jamsil Baseball Stadium. The Twins absorbed a 13-1 loss to the visiting Kia Tigers in Game 3 of the first round in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason Tuesday. It completed the Tigers' three-game sweep of the best-of-five battle and ended the Twins' bid for their second straight Korean Series title. It also ended up being the last official game played at Jamsil, which opened in 1982 and will be demolished after this season to make room for a new dome. Jamsil has been home to many memorable championship moments over the years, with the Twins and another club, Doosan Bears, as co-tenants. Most recently, the Twins clinched the 2023 Korean Series championship at Jamsil, their first title since 1994.

results.title: With massive homer in clinching game, Tigers superstar Kim Do-yeong voted KBO postseason series
results.content: With each passing game and each ball leaving the yard, Kia Tigers slugger Kim Do-yeong keeps growing in his stature as a clutch performer. Kim made an emphatic statement on his greatness Tuesday, as he hammered a grand slam to power the Tigers past the LG Twins 13-1 in Game 3 of their best-of-five Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason series. His blast capped a seven-run second inning for the Tigers, who cruised to an easy win to complete their three-game sweep. Kim, who finished the series with three home runs and eight RBIs in three games, was voted the series MVP. He collected 84 out of 97 votes for the honor. The Tigers were already up 3-0 when Kim stepped into the box in the top of the second, and things were unraveling quickly for the Twins. results.title: Raw fish replaces fried chicken as Seoul's new Han River picnic craze
results.content: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. A new trend known as “hoe-cnic” — a combination of "hoe," the Korean word for raw fish, and picnic — is gaining popularity along the Han River. Replacing fried chicken, long a staple of riverside outings, fresh raw fish is emerging as a new food trend in Seoul. A typical hoe-cnic outing begins with picking up takeout sashimi at Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market before heading to destinations such as Yeouido Hangang Park, Nodeulseom Island or Yanghwa Hangang Park. Participants often pair their raw fish with instant noodles cooked at the riverside or alcoholic drinks, and some rent picnic mats, tables or tents to create the perfect outdoor setting. results.title: After 20 years in acting, Jung Il-woo ventures into film investment, distribution
results.content: Actor Jung Il-woo has added another title to his resume: film investor. After expanding his presence beyond Korea into markets across Asia, including China, Japan and Vietnam, he is broadening his scope by investing in and distributing films. His goal is to use the name and experience he has built over 20 years to introduce good films to audiences. At this year's Busan International Film Festival, Jung was invited as a guest to Japanese Cinema Night, where he added star power to the event. Having appeared in numerous Japanese productions, he took on a role that went beyond the boundaries of Korea and Japan, helping share films and foster cultural exchange as part of the global film community.
